source.title: Taxonomizing local versus global structure in neural network loss landscapes
source.authors: Yaoqing Yang; Liam Hodgkinson; Ryan Theisen; Joe Zou; Joseph E. Gonzalez; K. Ramchandran; Michael W. Mahoney

record.tranche_reason: The study directly sweeps deep-network width and training-set size and measures test accuracy, reporting double descent in these settings. The study uses its own experimental setup rather than an explicit replication.
record.gate_note: The paper explicitly reports width-wise double descent and double descent as training-set size varies. The reported plots show test accuracy rather than test error, and the relevant curve values are figure-only. The paper does not report an epoch-wise double-descent result. Other loss-landscape metrics and findings that do not measure the claim’s risk curves are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study sweeps ResNet18 width on CIFAR-10 with 10% randomized labels and reports test-accuracy double descent, as in the original setup. It also reports width-wise double descent for Transformers on IWSLT De-En and compares runs with and without label noise. The framing is loss-landscape phases, but the risk curves themselves are measured.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors report width-wise and temperature-wise double descent with 10% noisy labels (ResNet18, Transformers). They interpret it as a 'bad fluctuation' at the transition between learning phases, and claim empirical double descent is a consequence of these phases. For the sample-size plots, they say double descent appears with and without noisy labels, but also that more data gives better accuracy overall.
record.recipe_differences: The paper directly sweeps network width and training-set size and evaluates test accuracy, but uses its own loss-landscape and phase-diagram experimental setup rather than explicitly reproducing the original protocol.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported curves vary with width, batch size or learning rate, training-set size, and whether 10% of labels are randomized. The paper also reports double descent with and without noisy labels.

fits_no_version.finding: Test accuracy shows 'temperature-wise' double descent as batch size or learning rate varies at fixed width (Fig 4a, 17a, 18).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Double descent along an SGD-noise (temperature) axis such as batch size or learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: The double-descent band coincides with transitions in Hessian eigenvalue/trace and mode connectivity between learning phases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The double-descent peak marks a transition between loss-landscape phases (locally sharp to flat; poorly- to well-connected).

record.problems: The relevant risk-curve values are presented in figures without numerical extraction in the text. The paper reports averages over five independent runs generally, but provides no uncertainty estimates for these curves in the supplied text. The stated results do not directly locate the interpolation threshold.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows were retained for the paper’s other loss-landscape measures, which do not themselves measure the claim’s specified test-risk curves. The epoch-wise claim is not reported as a result.

untested.parts: No epoch-wise test-error curves are reported.
Only deep networks (ResNet18, VGG11, Transformer) are studied.
No effective-complexity measure predicting peak location is tested.

Splitting into triple or multiple peaks, and removal of the peak under optimally tuned regularization, are not tested. Early stopping improves test accuracy (Fig 19), but the double-descent curve is not shown being removed.
Complexity is not recounted with an effective number of parameters.
Whether more samples raise test error near the threshold is not clearly shown (see r3/r4).

missing.what: Width-wise double descent in test CE loss for Transformers on IWSLT16 De-En
Clean-label width sweep (Fig 2a) shows no dark band, while 10% noisy labels (Fig 4a) shows double descent
missing.locator: Section 3.2, 'Training to noisy labels and double descent'; Figures 2a, 4a

missing.what: Optimal early stopping significantly improves test accuracy in the Transformer setting (the text cites [41] for early stopping mitigating double descent)

record.verdict_notes: V3 gets no verdict: the sample-size statement does not identify the axis of the non-monotonicity, and no numbers are given. All double-descent evidence is figure-only, averaged over five runs, with no uncertainty reported. There is no data augmentation and training uses a constant learning rate by default.

versions.untested_parts: The reported width sweeps use ResNet18 on CIFAR-10; other deep-network settings are not established by these rows.
Test error over training epochs following a fall-rise-fall curve.
The paper does not locate a specific interpolation threshold or quantify the size of the test-error increase.
Double descent across model classes beyond the deep networks studied.
A single effective-complexity measure predicting peak location across size, epochs, and samples.
Whether label noise or variance causes the peak; whether peaks split into triple or multiple descent; and whether optimally tuned regularization removes the peak.
Recounting complexity using effective parameters to determine whether the second descent becomes an ordinary U-shaped curve.
